title: feat(drilling): fine boring cycle (G76) with a required shift
body:
Stacked on #2823 (merge #2823 first).

## What changed

Fine boring is a new cycle on the drilling operation. This is the last slice of #1445, and it is the work of #1479.

- `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }` is a new cycle choice. The shift is a required part of the choice. There is no default shift.
- `CycleKind::FineBore` is a new CL cycle kind. The `.cl` text writes `FineBore`. The `.cnc` stream writes `CYCLE FINEBORE`.
- The chain of one hole is: feed in, shift at the bottom, rapid out at the shifted XY, shift back at R.
- The post engine reads the shift from the chain. It gives the shift to the script as `ShiftX` and `ShiftY`.
- The post engine refuses the cycle by name for a script that does not declare `fineBoring = true`.
- The Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole. It never writes `Q`.
- Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
- A machine file can state `spindle.orientation`. The value `false` refuses a fine bore with any post.
- The generator refuses a shift that the bar has no room for. The room is `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`.
- The commands refuse a zero shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift that is not smaller than a hole radius.
- The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped bar. It still reads the shank and the holder at the shifted position.
- The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, as it does for a bore and a ream.
- The project file, MCP `edit_operation` and the Cycle combo of the drill page carry the choice and its shift.

A program that does not choose the cycle posts the same bytes as before.

## Cause

Hole making had no fine boring cycle. A bore cycle rapids out with the tip on the wall, and the tip marks the finished bore.

## Design

- The shift is in the chain, not in a new record field. The posted `I` and `J` are the shift of the chain, so the two cannot disagree. The WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and the cycle centre together.
- The refusal for a post is in the engine. A new post is refused until it declares the flag.
- Haas `G76` reads `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y. The `Q` form takes its direction from Setting 27. A program cannot state that setting, so the post never writes `Q`.
- Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan take the direction of `Q` from a control parameter. These posts refuse. #2886 has the work for these controls, for Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, for Sinumerik `CYCLE86` and for Mach4.
- The verifier models the tool as the cylinder that the turning edge sweeps. That cylinder, shifted by `s`, enters the bore wall by `s`. With the spindle stopped, the bar reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches `tool radius - s`. The two stay inside the cylinder that the feed in cut while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over the same cylinder.
- The shank and the holder are not inside that cylinder. The solid law reads them at the shifted position.
- `docs/decisions/1445-fine-boring.md` has the options that were dropped.

MCP: `edit_operation` takes `"cycle": {"fine_bore": {"shift_x": 0.3, "shift_y": -0.4}}` (millimetres). The word `"fine_bore"` with no shift is refused.

## Tests

Pins:

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_fine_bore` (6 tests): the chain, the choice with no default, the room door, the bore door.
- `camcraft-post`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the stream word, the Haas `G76` block, the `P0` word, the refusal with no shift, the output-unit refusal, the refusal of each other post, the machine gate, the file word, the golden.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::fine_bore` (5 tests): the acquittal, the cases that keep each conviction, the holder that is still read, the holder collisions that the full verifier preserves.
- `camcraft-app`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the command with undo and redo, the project file, the `.cl` text, the stamp, the command doors, the generator door, the shank fit, the Haas post, the machine gate, the post refusal, MCP.
- `camcraft-ui` lib, `egui_app::tests::cycle_combo` (3 tests) and `egui_app::tests::holes_fine_bore` (2 tests).

Red before the change: the pins do not compile on the base. `CycleChoice::fine_bore`, `CycleKind::FineBore` and `fine_bore_gate` do not exist there. This is a new cycle, so there is no old behaviour to show red at run time. The first run of the app pin on the new generator, before the verifier change, was red:

```text
the verifier accepts the shifted retract: [RapidInStock { at: 2 }, RapidInStock { at: 3 }]
post blocked - 2 warning(s): FineBore1: rapid move 2 travels through stock ...; FineBore1: rapid move 3 travels through stock ...
```

Mutations. Each one was red with the guard removed and green after the restore:

| Guard removed | Pin that went red |
|---|---|
| motion: the room door (`s >= room`) | `a_shift_the_bar_has_no_room_for_is_refused_by_name` |
| motion: the zero shift at the choice | `the_fine_bore_choice_has_no_default_shift` |
| motion: the zero shift at the generator | `a_hand_made_zero_shift_is_refused_by_the_generator` |
| motion: the rapid out put back on the hole axis | `fine_bore_shifts_off_the_wall_before_the_rapid_out` |
| post engine: the `fineBoring` gate | `every_other_post_refuses_a_fine_bore_by_name` |
| post engine: the refusal with no shift | `a_fine_bore_with_no_shift_in_its_chain_is_refused_by_name` |
| Haas: the refusal with no shift | `a_fine_bore_with_no_shift_in_its_chain_is_refused_by_name` |
| Haas: the chain suppression at the shifted XY | `haas_writes_g76_with_the_shift_of_the_chain` |
| Haas: the `I` and `J` words | `haas_writes_g76_with_the_shift_of_the_chain` |
| machine: `fine_bore_gate` | `a_machine_that_cannot_stop_oriented_refuses_a_fine_bore` |
| machine: `spindle.orientation` must be a boolean | `spindle_orientation_must_be_a_boolean_or_the_file_is_refused` |
| verifier: the room in the acquittal | `a_shift_with_no_room_for_the_bar_keeps_every_conviction` |
| verifier: the chain shape in the acquittal | `a_group_that_is_not_the_cycles_chain_keeps_every_conviction` |
| verifier: the holder reading in the solid law | `the_solid_law_skips_the_stopped_edge_and_still_reads_the_shifted_holder` |
| verifier: the acquittal call in law (d) | `fine_bore_is_an_undoable_drill_parameter_that_generates_the_shift_and_round_trips` |
| app: the door in `CreateOperation` | `a_fine_bore_with_no_usable_shift_is_refused_when_the_command_is_made` |
| app: the door in `EditOperationParams` | `a_fine_bore_with_no_usable_shift_is_refused_when_the_command_is_made` |
| app: the shift in the digest | `the_shift_is_in_the_operation_stamp` |
| app: the machine gate call | `a_fine_bore_on_a_machine_that_cannot_stop_oriented_is_refused_by_name` |
| app: the fine bore in the shank-fit list of the reach law | `a_fine_bore_is_held_to_the_shank_fit_not_to_the_flute` |

Historical author gate on head `fd5767af0`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 936 steps, 0 failed, 61.8 minutes. The diff touches the shared `cl` crate, so the quick tier ran as the batch tier: each debug suite of geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui, and clippy.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.

## Review fixes

- The fine-bore acquittal filters only law (d) warnings. It preserves the solid-law holder collisions.
- The Haas post refuses a shift when both I and J round to zero in the output unit. It emits no G76 for that case.
- `verify::fine_bore::tests::the_full_verifier_keeps_the_shifted_holder_collisions` checks the public verifier. It checks shifts toward and away from the holder block.
- `haas_refuses_a_fine_bore_shift_that_rounds_to_zero_in_inch_output` checks the inch refusal on either axis. It also checks representable metric and inch shifts.

Review head: `c16ca2977db21332b6c810447ed083b74227d3dc`.

Both new pins passed before each mutation. Each pin failed with its source fix removed and passed after the fix was restored. The verifier mutation restored the old acquittal placement. The post mutation removed the formatted-zero guard.

Final-head checks on `c16ca2977db21332b6c810447ed083b74227d3dc`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. The gate ran 936 steps, with zero failures, in 81.5 minutes. The log directory is `gate-logs/quick-20261120-142823`.
- The gate clippy step: PASS, 193 seconds.
- Explicit clippy for `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: PASS, 14.67 seconds. It used `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- The UI library suite: 1,278 passed, 7 ignored, zero failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: PASS. The motion and app lanes ran 217 steps, with zero failures, in 59.3 minutes. The gate checked both `#1950` known-fail pins. Both failed as expected.
- `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots --only 'kernel heavy'`: PASS. The supplemental kernel lane ran 13 steps, with zero failures, in 6.6 minutes. The log directory is `gate-logs/release-20261120-164953`.

## UI screenshots

The screenshots use the same shell fixture. The before image uses the pre-PR drill page with the Bore cycle. The after image uses the new Fine bore cycle with Shift X 0.3 mm and Shift Y -0.4 mm. The images are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

![Before: pre-PR drill page with the Bore cycle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/cc499a0ba118d918dcd4bc8672ac1e75d6eae61c/2893/before.png)

![After: Fine bore with the explicit X and Y shifts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/cc499a0ba118d918dcd4bc8672ac1e75d6eae61c/2893/after.png)

## Goldens moved

One new golden: `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/haas.nc`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` file changed (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` lists this file only).

The cycle lines of the new golden:

```text
G99
G76 X10. Y10. Z-12. R2. I0.3 J-0.4 P500 F60
G80
```

## Not exercised

- No literature search ran. The session had no web access. No manual page was read in this session. Check the Haas `G76` block (`I`, `J`, `P`) against the Haas Mill Operator's Manual before a real cut.
- Nothing ran on a real control.
- The posted shift under a WCS flip, a WCS yaw or an inverted axis has no test of its own. The shift is read from moves that these transforms already change.
- The tip direction is the statement of the user. No test or check can prove it.
- The Machines sheet has no row for `spindle.orientation`. No shipped machine file states it (#2886).
- The UI screenshots use the shipping shell in the UI test harness. No native application window was started.
- A fine bore with the holder near a wall is read by the solid law only (the part). The fixture laws read the holder at the chain positions as before, and have no fine bore test.

## Overlaps

- #2823 changes the same function, `camcraft_motion::drilling::cycle::drill` (the Back bore arm and the dwell list). This PR is stacked on it and adds the fine bore arm and one entry in the same dwell list.
- #2831, #2833, #2836, #2716 and #2714 change `crates/app/src/project/params.rs` and `params_impl.rs` in other operation kinds. #2821 and #2024 change `crates/app/src/project/entity.rs` in other types. #2763 changes `crates/sim/src/sim.rs`, which this PR does not change. Each touches the same file, a different function. The PR that merges second takes a refresh.
- #2646, #2515 and #2506 add new posts. They do not declare `fineBoring`, so the engine refuses a fine bore for them with no change.

Effort: high

Changelog: Drilling has a fine boring cycle (G76 on Haas) with a required shift off the wall; other posts refuse it by name, and a machine that cannot stop its spindle oriented refuses it.

Fixes #1479
Fixes #1445
